tagline: Europe's most successful commuter river already carries 10M+ trips a year on diesel catamarans — the question isn't whether the river works, it's replacing diesel with a tier that's clean AND faster.
summary: London runs the most successful commuter river service in Europe. Uber Boat by Thames Clippers carries 10M+ passenger trips a year along the tidal Thames between Putney/Battersea and Woolwich/Barking Riverside, calling at ~24 piers and integrated into the Transport for London (TfL) network with contactless/Oyster. The fleet is fast diesel catamarans, and the pressures are converging: the Mayor's net-zero / clean-air agenda points squarely at decarbonizing the river fleet, the busiest central legs are frequency-constrained, and conventional electric river-buses are slow against the Thames's strong tides. A foiling-electric platform flies above the current at 30+ kts, silent and zero-wake past historic embankments, meets the clean-air mandate, and opens the longer estuary corridors diesel runs slowly today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire tideway commuter network — Putney/Battersea↔Westminster↔Canary Wharf↔Greenwich↔Woolwich/Barking Riverside (~16 nm end-to-end), plus the Gravesend/Tilbury extension — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with terminal charging; foils retract for displacement transit under the central bridges.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 2,000 nm hybrid range covers the estuary line-haul to Southend and the Kent/Essex coast (~40 nm) with no charging-infrastructure dependency — reopening corridors diesel runs slowly today.

competitive_landscape: The river is run today by Uber Boat by Thames Clippers (fast diesel catamarans) under TfL River Services, with the Port of London Authority as navigation authority. The network is proven and integrated, but the fleet is diesel and the central legs are frequency-constrained. There is no foiling incumbent — the opening is to be the clean, faster tier that turns the clean-air mandate into a better commute.
seasonality: Operable year-round; binding variables are strong tidal currents (~4–5 kts), winter wind-over-tide chop and reduced winter daylight. Foiling above the current is a direct advantage. No cyclone exposure.
regulatory_note: Transport for London (TfL) River Services integrates piers + ticketing; the Port of London Authority (PLA) is the navigation authority (speed/wake byelaws, licensing); the Maritime & Coastguard Agency (MCA) handles vessel certification. The tidal-Thames wake regime + heritage-embankment sensitivities make zero-wake foiling a positive differentiator.
signature_routes: Central London ↔ Southend / Kent coast (estuary hybrid line-haul, ~40 nm)

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of inter-island mobility at national scale — the proof that a foiling fleet can be the transport layer, not a novelty.
